title: ball_sahi_hurt_test
ranking_note: SAHI combos most likely to hurt (theory + measured recover-always)
page_note: These are the SAHI stacks most likely to hurt — recover-always, loose thr, no size filter, dense tiles, and SAHI piled with TTA/multiscale/Kalman/ByteTrack. Same P10 Top Left clip as ball_postprocessing_test. Not a gold rescore.

variants.title: 1. SAHI recover-always
variants.why: Measured hurt on train/gold — extra FPs; gold P_emit dropped.

variants.title: 2. SAHI always + topk=3
variants.why: Always tiles then keep 3 boxes — more room for tile junk.

variants.title: 3. SAHI always + topk=5
variants.why: Even looser topk — second/third FPs more likely to survive.

variants.title: 4. SAHI always + thr 0.20
variants.why: Lower detect floor on fullframe and tiles — weak false balls.

variants.title: 5. SAHI always, no size filter
variants.why: Drops geometry gate — huge/tiny junk from tiles can pass.

variants.title: 6. SAHI always + multiscale 1.5×
variants.why: Two recover paths at once — train already showed multiscale +FPs.

variants.title: 7. SAHI always + HFlip TTA
variants.why: TTA + always-tile: most aggressive recover; FP risk stacks.

variants.title: 8. SAHI always + Kalman
variants.why: Kalman coasts wrong tile dets across frames (gold R/P both hurt).

variants.title: 9. SAHI always + ByteTrack (no emit gate)
variants.why: Sticky tracks on tile FPs — junk can linger without 0.80 gate.

variants.title: 10. Dense SAHI tiles (640 / 40% overlap) + topk=3
variants.why: More/smaller tiles → more false peaks; keep three of them.
